passages.text: My son, if you have put up security for your neighbor, if you have struck hands in pledge with a stranger, if you have been trapped by the words of your lips, ensnared by the words of your mouth, then do this, my son, to free yourself, for you have fallen into your neighbor’s hands: Go, humble yourself, and press your plea with your neighbor.
passages.sermon:
My son, listen carefully.
If you have promised to pay your neighbor’s debt, pay attention.
If you have made a pledge for a stranger, understand this.
If you have been trapped by your own words, know it.
If your mouth has ensnared you, realize it.
You are now in your neighbor’s power.
Do this, my son, to save yourself.
Go quickly to your neighbor.
Humble yourself before him.
Plead with your neighbor to release you.
passages.original: בְּ֭נִי אִם־ עָרַ֣בְתָּ לְרֵעֶ֑ךָ תָּקַ֖עְתָּ לַזָּ֣ר כַּפֶּֽיךָ׃ נוֹקַ֥שְׁתָּ בְאִמְרֵי־ פִ֑יךָ נִ֝לְכַּ֗דְתָּ בְּאִמְרֵי־ פִֽיךָ׃ עֲשֵׂ֨ה זֹ֥את אֵפ֪וֹא׀ בְּנִ֡י וְֽהִנָּצֵ֗ל כִּ֘י בָ֤אתָ בְכַף־ רֵעֶ֑ךָ לֵ֥ךְ הִ֝תְרַפֵּ֗ס וּרְהַ֥ב רֵעֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Allow no sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids.
passages.sermon: Do not let your eyes sleep.\r\nDo not let your eyelids slumber.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּתֵּ֣ן שֵׁנָ֣ה לְעֵינֶ֑יךָ וּ֝תְנוּמָ֗ה לְעַפְעַפֶּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler.
passages.sermon:
A person can fall into danger by making unwise promises or pledges.
You must act quickly to escape.
Free yourself from trouble.
Be like a gazelle that escapes from the hunter’s hand.
Be like a bird that escapes from the snare of the fowler.
Do not wait.
Act now to save yourself.
passages.original: הִ֭נָּצֵל כִּצְבִ֣י מִיָּ֑ד וּ֝כְצִפּ֗וֹר מִיַּ֥ד יָקֽוּשׁ׃פ

passages.text: Walk in the manner of the ant, O slacker; observe its ways and become wise.
passages.sermon:
The writer addresses a lazy person.
He calls this person a slacker.
He gives a command to the slacker.
He tells the slacker to go to the ant.
He tells the slacker to observe the ant’s ways.
He tells the slacker to learn from the ant.
He says the slacker will become wise by doing this.
passages.original: לֵֽךְ־ אֶל־ נְמָלָ֥ה עָצֵ֑ל רְאֵ֖ה דְרָכֶ֣יהָ וַחֲכָֽם׃

passages.text: Without a commander, without an overseer or ruler, it prepares its provisions in summer; it gathers its food at harvest.
passages.sermon:
The ant has no commander.
The ant has no overseer.
The ant has no ruler.
The ant prepares its food in summer.
The ant gathers its food at harvest.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֵֽין־ לָ֥הּ קָצִ֗ין שֹׁטֵ֥ר וּמֹשֵֽׁל׃ תָּכִ֣ין בַּקַּ֣יִץ לַחְמָ֑הּ אָגְרָ֥ה בַ֝קָּצִ֗יר מַאֲכָלָֽהּ׃

passages.text: How long will you lie there, O slacker? When will you get up from your sleep?
passages.sermon:
A lazy person lies down for a long time.
The lazy person does not get up quickly.
How long will you stay lying there, lazy person?
When will you rise from your sleep?
passages.original: עַד־ מָתַ֖י עָצֵ֥ל׀ תִּשְׁכָּ֑ב מָ֝תַ֗י תָּק֥וּם מִשְּׁנָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest, and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit.
passages.sermon:
This passage warns a lazy person about the danger of idleness.
A lazy person sleeps a little.
A lazy person slumbers a little.
A lazy person folds his hands to rest.
Poverty comes quickly to a lazy person.
Poverty comes like a robber.
Need comes to a lazy person.
Need comes like a bandit.
passages.original: מְעַ֣ט שֵׁ֭נוֹת מְעַ֣ט תְּנוּמ֑וֹת מְעַ֓ט׀ חִבֻּ֖ק יָדַ֣יִם לִשְׁכָּֽב׃ וּבָֽא־ כִמְהַלֵּ֥ךְ רֵאשֶׁ֑ךָ וּ֝מַחְסֹֽרְךָ֗ כְּאִ֣ישׁ מָגֵֽן׃פ

passages.text: A worthless person, a wicked man, walks with a perverse mouth, winking his eyes, speaking with his feet, and pointing with his fingers.
passages.sermon:
A worthless person acts with evil intent.
A wicked man speaks twisted words.
He walks with a perverse mouth.
He winks with his eyes.
He signals with his feet.
He points with his fingers.
passages.original: אָדָ֣ם בְּ֭לִיַּעַל אִ֣ישׁ אָ֑וֶן ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ עִקְּשׁ֥וּת פֶּֽה׃ קֹרֵ֣ץ בְּ֭עֵינָו מֹלֵ֣ל בְּרַגְלָ֑ו מֹ֝רֶ֗ה בְּאֶצְבְּעֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: With deceit in his heart he devises evil; he continually sows discord.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man has deceit in his heart.
He plans evil at all times.
He always causes conflict.
He spreads discord among people.
passages.original: תַּֽהְפֻּכ֨וֹת׀ בְּלִבּ֗וֹ חֹרֵ֣שׁ רָ֣ע בְּכָל־ עֵ֑ת מְדָנִים יְשַׁלֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: Therefore calamity will come upon him suddenly; in an instant he will be shattered beyond recovery.
passages.sermon:
A worthless and wicked man acts with deceit and causes trouble.
Suddenly, disaster will strike him.
He will be broken instantly.
No one will be able to heal him.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֗ן פִּ֭תְאֹם יָב֣וֹא אֵיד֑וֹ פֶּ֥תַע יִ֝שָּׁבֵ֗ר וְאֵ֣ין מַרְפֵּֽא׃פ

passages.text: There are six things that the LORD hates, seven that are detestable to Him: haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood, a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that run swiftly to evil, a false witness who gives false testimony, and one who stirs up discord among brothers.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD hates six things.
Seven things are detestable to Him.
He hates haughty eyes.
He hates a lying tongue.
He hates hands that shed innocent blood.
He hates a heart that devises wicked schemes.
He hates feet that run quickly to do evil.
He hates a false witness who gives false testimony.
He hates a person who stirs up discord among brothers.
passages.original: שֶׁשׁ־ הֵ֭נָּה שָׂנֵ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וְ֝שֶׁ֗בַע תּוֹעֲבוֹת נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃ עֵינַ֣יִם רָ֭מוֹת לְשׁ֣וֹן שָׁ֑קֶר וְ֝יָדַ֗יִם שֹׁפְכ֥וֹת דָּם־ נָקִֽי׃ לֵ֗ב חֹ֭רֵשׁ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת אָ֑וֶן רַגְלַ֥יִם מְ֝מַהֲר֗וֹת לָר֥וּץ לָֽרָעָה׃ יָפִ֣יחַ כְּ֭זָבִים עֵ֣ד שָׁ֑קֶר וּמְשַׁלֵּ֥חַ מְ֝דָנִ֗ים בֵּ֣ין אַחִֽים׃פ

passages.text: My son, keep your father’s commandment, and do not forsake your mother’s teaching.
passages.sermon:
A father gives commandments to his son.
A mother gives teachings to her son.
A son must keep his father’s commandment.
A son must not forsake his mother’s teaching.
passages.original: נְצֹ֣ר בְּ֭נִי מִצְוַ֣ת אָבִ֑יךָ וְאַל־ תִּ֝טֹּ֗שׁ תּוֹרַ֥ת אִמֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Bind them always upon your heart; tie them around your neck.
passages.sermon:
A father gives commandments. 
A mother gives teaching. 
These commandments and teachings are important. 
Keep them close to you at all times. 
Hold them in your heart always. 
Tie them around your neck. 
Let them stay with you wherever you go.
passages.original: קָשְׁרֵ֣ם עַל־ לִבְּךָ֣ תָמִ֑יד עָ֝נְדֵ֗ם עַל־ גַּרְגְּרֹתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: When you walk, they will guide you; when you lie down, they will watch over you; when you awake, they will speak to you.
passages.sermon:
A father’s commandment and a mother’s teaching are important.
These teachings guide you.
When you walk, they lead you.
When you lie down, they protect you.
When you wake up, they speak to you.
passages.original: בְּהִתְהַלֶּכְךָ֨׀ תַּנְחֶ֬ה אֹתָ֗ךְ בְּֽ֭שָׁכְבְּךָ תִּשְׁמֹ֣ר עָלֶ֑יךָ וַ֝הֲקִיצ֗וֹתָ הִ֣יא תְשִׂיחֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: For this commandment is a lamp, this teaching is a light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way to life, to keep you from the evil woman, from the smooth tongue of the adulteress.
passages.sermon:
God gives commandments.
Each commandment is like a lamp.
God gives teaching.
Each teaching is like a light.
Reproofs of discipline show the way to life.
These things protect you.
They keep you from the evil woman.
They guard you from the smooth tongue of the adulteress.
passages.original: כִּ֤י נֵ֣ר מִ֭צְוָה וְת֣וֹרָה א֑וֹר וְדֶ֥רֶךְ חַ֝יִּ֗ים תּוֹכְח֥וֹת מוּסָֽר׃ לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ מֵאֵ֣שֶׁת רָ֑ע מֵֽ֝חֶלְקַ֗ת לָשׁ֥וֹן נָכְרִיָּֽה׃

passages.text: Do not lust in your heart for her beauty or let her captivate you with her eyes.
passages.sermon:
This passage warns against the temptation of an adulterous woman.
Do not desire her beauty in your heart.
Do not let her eyes capture you.
Guard your heart from longing for her.
Do not let her looks control you.
passages.original: אַל־ תַּחְמֹ֣ד יָ֭פְיָהּ בִּלְבָבֶ֑ךָ וְאַל־ תִּ֝קָּֽחֲךָ֗ בְּעַפְעַפֶּֽיהָ׃

passages.text: For the levy of the prostitute is poverty, and the adulteress preys upon your very life.
passages.sermon:
A prostitute takes away your money.
She leaves you with nothing but a loaf of bread.
An adulteress hunts for your precious life.
She seeks to destroy your soul.
passages.original: כִּ֤י בְעַד־ אִשָּׁ֥ה זוֹנָ֗ה עַֽד־ כִּכַּ֫ר לָ֥חֶם וְאֵ֥שֶׁת אִ֑ישׁ נֶ֖פֶשׁ יְקָרָ֣ה תָצֽוּד׃פ

passages.text: Can a man embrace fire and his clothes not be burned?
passages.sermon:
A man cannot hold fire close to his body.
His clothes will burn if he does this.
Fire always burns what touches it.
No one can embrace fire and remain unharmed.
passages.original: הֲיַחְתֶּ֤ה אִ֓ישׁ אֵ֬שׁ בְּחֵיק֑וֹ וּ֝בְגָדָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִשָּׂרַֽפְנָה׃

passages.text: Can a man walk on hot coals without scorching his feet?
passages.sermon:
A man walks on hot coals.
His feet touch the burning coals.
His feet will be burned.
No one can walk on hot coals and keep his feet from being scorched.
passages.original: אִם־ יְהַלֵּ֣ךְ אִ֭ישׁ עַל־ הַגֶּחָלִ֑ים וְ֝רַגְלָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִכָּוֶֽינָה׃

passages.text: So is he who sleeps with another man’s wife; no one who touches her will go unpunished.
passages.sermon: A man who sleeps with another man's wife commits adultery.\r\nHe will not escape punishment.\r\nAnyone who touches her will be punished.
passages.original: כֵּ֗ן הַ֭בָּא אֶל־ אֵ֣שֶׁת רֵעֵ֑הוּ לֹ֥א יִ֝נָּקֶ֗ה כָּֽל־ הַנֹּגֵ֥עַ בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: Men do not despise the thief if he steals to satisfy his hunger.
passages.sermon:
A thief may steal because he is hungry.
He wants to fill his stomach.
People do not despise this thief.
They understand his reason for stealing.
passages.original: לֹא־ יָב֣וּזוּ לַ֭גַּנָּב כִּ֣י יִגְנ֑וֹב לְמַלֵּ֥א נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ כִּ֣י יִרְעָֽב׃

passages.text: Yet if caught, he must pay sevenfold; he must give up all the wealth of his house.
passages.sermon:
A thief may steal because he is hungry.
If people catch the thief, they require him to pay back much more.
He must pay back seven times what he took.
He must give up all the wealth in his house.
passages.original: וְ֭נִמְצָא יְשַׁלֵּ֣ם שִׁבְעָתָ֑יִם אֶת־ כָּל־ ה֖וֹן בֵּית֣וֹ יִתֵּֽן׃

passages.text: He who commits adultery lacks judgment; whoever does so destroys himself.
passages.sermon:
A man who commits adultery lacks sense.
He does not have good judgment.
He destroys himself by this act.
He brings harm to his own life.
passages.original: נֹאֵ֣ף אִשָּׁ֣ה חֲסַר־ לֵ֑ב מַֽשְׁחִ֥ית נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ ה֣וּא יַעֲשֶֽׂנָּה׃

passages.text: Wounds and dishonor will befall him, and his reproach will never be wiped away.
passages.sermon:
A man who commits adultery will suffer.
He will receive wounds.
He will experience dishonor.
People will not forget his shame.
His disgrace will remain forever.
passages.original: נֶֽגַע־ וְקָל֥וֹן יִמְצָ֑א וְ֝חֶרְפָּת֗וֹ לֹ֣א תִמָּחֶֽה׃

passages.text: For jealousy enrages a husband, and he will show no mercy in the day of vengeance.
passages.sermon:
A husband can feel jealousy.
Jealousy makes a husband very angry.
A jealous husband will not show mercy.
He will not forgive on the day he takes revenge.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ קִנְאָ֥ה חֲמַת־ גָּ֑בֶר וְלֹֽא־ יַ֝חְמ֗וֹל בְּי֣וֹם נָקָֽם׃

passages.text: He will not be appeased by any ransom, or persuaded by lavish gifts.
passages.sermon:
A jealous husband will not accept any ransom.
He will not forgive because of any payment.
He will not agree even if you offer many gifts.
No amount of money or gifts will change his mind.
passages.original: לֹא־ יִ֭שָּׂא פְּנֵ֣י כָל־ כֹּ֑פֶר וְלֹֽא־ יֹ֝אבֶ֗ה כִּ֣י תַרְבֶּה־ שֹֽׁחַד׃פ
